import HartshorneLib.Chapter4DifferentialDivisor
import HartshorneLib.Chapter4DivisorClass

/-!
# The canonical divisor class of a smooth proper curve

The divisor attached to a nonzero rational differential depends on the chosen
differential, while its class modulo principal divisors does not.  This file
records that invariant without selecting a canonical differential.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Hartshorne

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
variable {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} [IsIntegral X.left]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom] [IsProper X.hom]

/-- The divisor class represented by the divisor of a chosen nonzero rational
differential.  The definition is choice-dependent; `canonicalDivisorClass_eq`
proves that its value is independent of that choice. -/
noncomputable def canonicalDivisorClass
    (ω : CurveRationalDifferentials X) (hω : ω ≠ 0) :
    DivisorClassGroup (k := k) (X := X) :=
  divisorClass (differentialDivisor X ω hω)

/-- Divisors of two nonzero rational differentials determine the same class. -/
theorem canonicalDivisorClass_eq
    (ω η : CurveRationalDifferentials X) (hω : ω ≠ 0) (hη : η ≠ 0) :
    canonicalDivisorClass (X := X) ω hω = canonicalDivisorClass η hη := by
  apply (linearlyEquivalent_iff_divisorClass_eq
    (differentialDivisor X ω hω) (differentialDivisor X η hη)).mp
  exact differentialDivisor_linearlyEquivalent X ω η hω hη

/-- There is a canonical divisor class, represented by every nonzero rational
differential.  No differential is selected by this existence statement. -/
theorem exists_canonicalDivisorClass :
    ∃ c : DivisorClassGroup (k := k) (X := X),
      ∀ (ω : CurveRationalDifferentials X) (hω : ω ≠ 0),
        canonicalDivisorClass (X := X) ω hω = c := by
  obtain ⟨ω, hω⟩ := exists_nonzero_curveRationalDifferential X
  refine ⟨canonicalDivisorClass (X := X) ω hω, ?_⟩
  intro η hη
  exact canonicalDivisorClass_eq (X := X) η ω hη hω

end
end Hartshorne
